title: Anne Sullivan's birth chart
metaDescription: Anne Sullivan's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 14.7° Aries. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Four of the nine placements whose signs are settled stand in Aries — the Sun, Mercury, Venus and Neptune. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Aries, but precisely: 14.7°, second decan, 10°–20°, under the Sun in the triplicity scheme. The tradition kept these divisions because thirty degrees is a long street.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Mercury at 28.6° Aries, Venus at 24.1° Aries, Mars at 7.3° Pisces. Mercury in a fire sign reads as a mind that decides at speaking speed; Venus in a fire sign reads as taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate; Mars in a water sign reads as drive that moves on certainty and current.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Mercury and Jupiter hold the closest angle here — a square, 0.5° wide. Right angles are where the scheme puts its grit. A square asks two functions to work in a mode neither would have chosen. Behind it, Mercury sextile Uranus at 1.5°, and Saturn opposition Pluto at 2.2° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, three sit in a sign it has an opinion about. The Sun in Aries at 14.7° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Venus in Aries at 24.1° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Jupiter in Capricorn at 29.1° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 4 fire, 3 water, 2 earth by element and 6 cardinal, 2 fixed, 1 mutable by mode. No settled placement falls in air — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Mercury and Saturn were retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Scorpio into Sagittarius during that day at the birthplace, travelling 11.9° between one midnight and the next. The hour would decide it; no hour was recorded. The reading keeps the question open rather than flipping a coin dressed as astrology.
